api:xmlFragment.en:
Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη (PPE).

Mr President, Commissioner, ladies and gentlemen, we have built peace. However, Russian violations of the airspace of the Union and repeated Turkish provocations against Greece and Cyprus send a clear message. Europe must defend itself. Military mobility, the foundation of a common European defence and security, will play a key role in shielding the Union and strengthening our deterrent capacity and, above all, our military autonomy. The Committee on Transport welcomes the legislative package and the tenfold increase in the proposed budget in the next multiannual framework.

There should be no cuts. Only adequate funding ensures modern dual-use infrastructure and the removal of administrative and technical barriers to the seamless transfer of equipment and personnel within the European Union. It also highlights the central role of ports as military mobility hubs and the need to upgrade them through increased funding.

Colleagues, defence and security in the Union are in our hands. We have a responsibility to respond to this historic challenge.

activity_label.en: Presentation of the programme of activities of the Cyprus Presidency (continuation of debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη (PPE).

Madam President, Commissioner, Mr President, welcome. The martyred Cyprus, which has endured illegal invasion and occupation for more than fifty years, is taking office at a critical time when the Union is suffering from geopolitical changes and dramatic conflicts. We must rise to the occasion dynamically, in response to the revisionist forces threatening our borders, with an autonomous common European defence policy.

In my Committee on Transport, we are working – to this end – on the necessary legislation on military mobility. At the same time, in the European Parliament, we are working intensively to meet key demands from European citizens, including air passenger rights, maritime safety, migration and improving the quality of life.

Mr. President of the Republic of Cyprus, good luck! We are confident that your leadership and determination will make a decisive contribution to our challenging work.

activity_label.en: Restoring control of migration: returns, visa policy and third-country cooperation (topical debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη (PPE).

Mr President, the new Pact on Asylum and Migration is a major European success. But it's not enough. There are new facts. For our migration policy to be credible, it must be complemented by an effective system of returns, without which it cannot be sustainable. A strong legal and operational framework, simplification of procedures and effective cooperation with third countries are needed. Where such cooperation does not work, concrete consequences should be envisaged. The Union should use all available tools to build strong and mutually beneficial relations to ensure the implementation of readmission decisions and to prevent irregular arrivals. Consider also setting up return centres outside Europe.

My country, Greece, a key gateway, has shown that effective border management is possible. In 2025 we had 13,000 fewer arrivals, while in December last year alone there were almost 1,000 returns, double the annual average. With uniform rules, a proportionate sharing of responsibilities for all members and a common system of returns, we can effectively protect our borders, strengthen the security of citizens and ensure fair, and above all humane, management of migration.

activity_label.en: Presentation of the action plan against cyberbullying (debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη (PPE).

Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, the action plan to combat cyberbullying is a crucial step in protecting young people online. Cyberbullying knows no limits, it's a scourge. It is reinforced by anonymity and is now a social pathogen with serious consequences for the mental health, dignity and lives of thousands of children and young people. When one in six young people is a victim, treatment is a one-way street. The criminalisation of cyberbullying with the cooperation of all Member States here and now. Above all, however, emphasis is needed on prevention and early intervention, as new technologies, such as artificial intelligence and virtual reality, are constantly emerging.

We must invest directly in the digital education of young people and parents and in the training of teachers. To guarantee a safe online environment for our children in the future. And platforms must finally be obliged to comply with the provisions stemming from the Digital Services Act on the protection of minors. They have a responsibility. Colleagues, we have intervened on cyberbullying with serious resolutions in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2025 with an own-initiative report. But the problem is present, it is evolving and it is very serious and dangerous. Tackling it effectively requires a combination of joint actions by all Member States. It is not a choice, it is our duty to young people and future generations.

activity_label.en: Commemoration of the genocide of Armenians and Greeks in Pontos and Asia Minor (debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη, on behalf of the Group PPE.

Mr President, ladies and gentlemen, today is a historic date. May 19th is for Greece the terrible memory of the systematic extermination of the Pontic Greeks. It is a day of national remembrance for the atrocities, torture, uprooting and annihilation of a thriving Greek population with a strong national identity from Turkey, which always consciously serves a revisionist policy of contempt for international law. Tragic events have been indelibly imprinted in world history and have long been a deep wound at the heart of humanism. Recording historical truth is a foundation for democracy. That is why the victims are asking for vindication stemming from the code of our European values.

Today we address the European Parliament, the leading democratic institution, with directly elected representatives from the millions of European citizens. We ask that he rise to the occasion, responding to a just and moral demand of all Greeks. We call on the European Union and all Member States to recognise the genocide of the Greeks of Pontus and Asia Minor. International recognition of genocide is a continuing duty to victims and future generations to preserve historical memory and defend democracy, peace and human dignity.

Ladies and gentlemen, today, when peace and security are being challenged by painful conflicts in our neighbourhood and unpredictable international circumstances, I ask you to join our voice with the just request of my country: Recognize the genocide of the Pontic Greeks. Recognition in itself is a serious act of responsibility and is the due resounding response to all those who despise international law, peace, freedom, justice and the value of human life.

Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη (PPE).

Mr President, the report on Turkey clearly reflects European concerns about the deterioration of human rights and violations of international law. Nevertheless, Turkey not only does not change its stance, but with constant provocative actions and statements, it promotes its revisionist policy and adheres to the doctrine of the blue homeland, while praising illegally occupied Cyprus.

At the same time, it attempts to challenge the sovereignty of 152 Greek islands, islets and rocky islets in the Aegean, and only on June 7 harassed transport aircraft of the defence ministers of Greece, France and the Netherlands travelling to Cyprus for the informal meeting of the European Union.

Colleagues, it has been shown that Turkey's behaviour does not produce progress. It consciously ignores resolutions, decisions and European ideals. We must safeguard our values and interests by now changing a policy that has failed, with new, brave decisions, even a review of the pre-accession funds. There is an urgent need to force Turkey to finally meet its obligations.

activity_label.en: Escalations in the Eastern Mediterranean and the Aegean following persistent Turkish provocations (debate)

api:xmlFragment.en:
Ελισσάβετ Βόζεμπεργκ-Βρυωνίδη, on behalf of the Group PPE.

Mr President, today's debate on Turkish provocations is not a repetition of previous ones. Turkey is daily escalating its provocative behavior towards Greece with continuous violations of airspace and actions that undermine security and stability in the region. On August 15, Ankara announced the establishment of two illegal marine parks in international waters and in an area within the Greek continental shelf. It immediately plans to legislate the Blue Homeland, challenging Greek sovereignty over 152 islands and islets in the Aegean. He was against the Greek prime minister who visited Kastelorizo and insists on illegal claims for the demilitarization of the Greek islands. It systematically threatens my country with war if it exercises its legal right to extend its territorial waters beyond 6 miles. And it went so far as to herald aggressive actions if the electrical interconnection between Greece and Cyprus proceeds without its permission.

I ask you colleagues, is Turkey a reliable strategic partner when it threatens Member States of the European Union? How do we respond to a revisionist force challenging the security and external borders of the Union, in defiance of international law?

Commissioner, today we rightly demand from the European Union serious sanctions against Turkey and an explicit statement that an attack on Greece is understood as an attack on the entire European family. Only as such can it be treated.
